source_meta._title: Recipes for new waxed copper blocks are not grouped

stor.environment: A vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 23w44a client running a local single-player world in Creative mode, with commands enabled, the Update 1.21 experiment enabled during world creation, and the game language set to English (US) so the report's literal recipe-book search text works.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make snapshot installations available, then install and launch Java Edition 23w44a. Confirm that the lower-left corner of the title screen identifies the running version as 23w44a.
Use an unmodified client without additional datapacks that alter recipes or recipe-book grouping.
A new world may be used; the report does not require a particular world seed, terrain, dimension, or coordinates.
Use keyboard and mouse controls. The instructions name default controls; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: From the 23w44a title screen, set the game language to English (US): open Options, open Language, select English (US), and confirm with Done until you return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title-screen interface is displayed in English, allowing the exact recipe-book query "waxed" to match the English recipe names.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World. Configure the new world to use Creative game mode and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. No particular seed is required, so leave the seed at its default random value.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Creative as the selected game mode and commands are allowed.

steps.action: Before creating the world, open the Experiments screen from the world-creation options. Turn on the experiment labeled Update 1.21, accept the experimental-feature warning if one appears, and return to the world-creation screen without disabling the experiment.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation interface indicates that the Update 1.21 experiment is enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate and enter the experimental world.
steps.success_cue: The player appears in the world and the normal in-game HUD is visible.

steps.action: Wait until world generation and nearby chunk loading are complete. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible or while terrain is still appearing around the player.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered and the player can look and move normally.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the report's recipe command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, then press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that recipes were granted to the player; recipe-unlock notifications may also begin appearing.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use its item search field to find a Crafting Table, then place one Crafting Table into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots shown at the bottom of the inventory and HUD.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table item is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Escape. Select the hotbar slot containing the Crafting Table by pressing its number key or scrolling the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The Crafting Table is visibly held in the player's main hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of a nearby solid block where there is empty space above it, then right-click once to place the Crafting Table.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table block is visible in the world directly at the targeted placement location.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the placed Crafting Table and right-click once to use it.
steps.success_cue: The 3-by-3 Crafting interface is open and the placed Crafting Table remains visible behind the interface if the background is not fully obscured.

steps.action: If the recipe-book panel is not visible on the left side of the Crafting interface, click the green recipe-book button beside the crafting grid to open it. If it is already visible, leave it open.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book panel, including its search field and recipe entries, is visible alongside the 3-by-3 crafting grid.

steps.action: In the recipe-book panel, select the general Search/All category, represented by the compass tab, so the search is not restricted to another recipe category. Also set the recipe filter to Showing All rather than Showing Craftable; hover over or click the filter button as needed to confirm its tooltip/state. This is necessary because the player is not carrying all recipe ingredients.
steps.success_cue: The compass Search/All tab is selected and the recipe-book filter reports Showing All.

steps.action: Click the recipe-book search field. Clear any existing text with Ctrl+A followed by Backspace, type the report's broad search query exactly, and leave the search results displayed without clicking or crafting a result.
steps.success_cue: The search field contains "waxed" and the recipe-book results have refreshed to entries whose English names match that search.

stor.handoff_condition: The Crafting Table interface and recipe-book panel are open, all recipes have been granted, the recipe filter is set to Showing All, and the recipe-book search has just refreshed for the query "waxed". Begin inspection of the displayed recipe entries and their grouping.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode or seed. Creative mode and a fresh random-seed world are practical choices that minimize unrelated item-acquisition work and do not change the recipe-book grouping action under test.

The report lists many affected releases, but 23w44a is recommended because it matches the original experiment-based instructions and retains the original set of Update 1.21 experimental copper recipes described by the reporter.

The report also suggests the narrower searches "waxed c", "waxed e", "waxed w", and "waxed o" for isolating regular, exposed, weathered, and oxidized results. The broad query "waxed" is used as the primary deterministic trigger; the observation subsystem may substitute one of those exact narrower queries if the full result list does not fit in the visible recipe-book panel.
Recipe-book button positions can shift with GUI scale and window size. The plan identifies controls by their icon, label, tooltip, and resulting state rather than relying on fixed screen coordinates.
